rules.title: Tenant Screening Fee Cap
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a capped screening fee to cover costs like a credit report, and must refund any unused portion, provide a receipt, and give a copy of the credit report within 7 days.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental applications statewide; fee must be tied to actual screening costs incurred.
rules.exemptions: No fee may be charged if no unit is actually available; fee must be refunded to applicants not selected unless a first-come, first-qualified policy is used.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96

rules.title: Notification of State Law Limitation on Tenant Screening Fees
rules.requirement: Before charging a screening fee, a Berkeley landlord must give applicants a clear statement of their tenant screening fee rights and the state maximum fee cap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when an owner or agent charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report or process a rental application in Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b).

rules.title: Prohibition of Non-Refundable Application Fees Associated with Existing Tenancies
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to add, replace, or handle the departure of a roommate.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to existing tenancies and roommate changes within a pre-existing household in Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
